html:
SMTO-EXE-0225 — SMTO couldn't find that Docker volume

GUID: ffb41291-3e0b-554d-9db0-98ab36ae0b34
Slug: docker-volume-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • No Docker volume (a storage area where Docker keeps a container's data) with exactly that name exists on the Gateway computer right now. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the Docker volumes on that Gateway, and check the exact spelling of the name you used. Volume names must match exactly; SMTO won't guess a close match.
  2. Check that you picked the Gateway for the computer where the volume was created. Each computer's Docker keeps its own volumes, and SMTO only looks on the Gateway you selected.
  3. Only if the volume truly doesn't exist and your task needs one, ask SMTO to create a new volume with that name. SMTO never creates a volume on its own, and a new volume starts empty.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the volume by its exact name and the action continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the volume name, to the person who manages Docker on that computer. Don't create a new volume to replace one you expected to hold data; it won't contain that data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exact volume resolution on the Gateway found no volume with the requested name, or the Docker Engine returned 404 on a /volumes endpoint.

What this means

  • Exact volume lookup found no matching name, or the Engine returned a volume-path not-found response. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exact volume lookup found no matching name, or the Engine returned a volume-path not-found response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the intended Engine's volume list and any earlier creation/removal receipt.

How to fix it

  • List volumes on the same Gateway (docker volume ls as the Gateway account) and pass the exact volume name. Create a volume only through an explicit volume_create when the task needs a new one, after confirming the selected Gateway is the host that holds the data.
  • Select the exact existing volume, or separately authorize creation only if the task requires a new one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended volume name resolves before mounting or removal.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
